question: Which 3-win to open-class promotion horses show evidence that stronger opposition elicits more of their latent output?

engine_profile.definition: previous-race RPCI >= 50 AND previous-race final-3F at least 0.5 sec faster than that race field median
engine_profile.meaning: back-loaded/slow-side race shape plus clearly superior relative late speed
engine_profile.note: This is intentionally a simple interpretable profile, not a fitted seconds correction.

heldout_probability_model.interpretation: Calibration losses improve slightly but the paired holdout confidence intervals cross zero, so this is not yet strong enough for a hard probability correction.

strict_clock_sensitivity.condition: same venue, surface, exact distance, course division and going between 3-win and open starts
strict_clock_sensitivity.sign_convention: positive = horse itself ran faster after promotion
strict_clock_sensitivity.interpretation: Suggestive but small-n and unstable; it is notable that the profile mean is close to +0.2 sec, but this is not precise enough to justify a universal +0.2-sec correction.

model_search.continuous_engine_features: Adding RPCI, PCI-RPCI, relative final-3F, remaining-600m gap and position to a regularized performance model produced only a modest 2025-2026 gain (Spearman about 0.246 -> 0.278; MAE about 0.538 -> 0.531), with paired bootstrap uncertainty crossing zero.
model_search.nearby_threshold_sensitivity: RPCI thresholds 49-51 and relative final-3F thresholds 0.4-0.6 sec generally preserved a positive top-3 lift, suggesting the signal is not dependent on one exact cut point.

decision.recommended_label: 昇級エンジン候補 β
decision.recommended_use: context/ranking-support only; do not alter win/top2/top3 probabilities or FinishScore yet
